notes.decision: Translated 'the bitter [one]' from ⲥⲏϣⲉ/ⲥⲓϣⲉ 'be bitter, gall.' The gustatory register is established by the immediately preceding ⲧϯⲡⲉ 'the taste,' fitting the Manichaean correspondential schema where the realm of the five spirits of darkness has a bitter taste (cf. ⲡϣⲏⲛ ⲉⲧⲍⲁⲩ 'the bitter tree'). Alternative ⲥⲁϣⲉ 'stripe, blow' would yield 'the lash' but does not fit the gustatory parallelism.

Read as Lycopolitan reduction of Greek ⲃⲁⲥⲁⲛⲟⲥ (βάσανος) 'torment, trial, ordeal.' Translated 'the torment.' The pairing with 'taste' and 'fruit' suggests this is the gustatory-experiential register of the dark spirits' work.

Translated 'the foretellers,' parsing as ⲛⲉⲧ-ϣⲁ(ⲣⲡ̄)-ⲣⲧ or related to ϣⲣ̄ⲡ 'first, before' = those who do something in advance, hence prognosticators. Parallel to ⲣⲉϥϯⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'sign-givers' and 'spirits which inquire,' all in a divinatory list. Alternative readings considered: 'those who tremble' (ecstatics), 'those who scatter (lots)' — none confirmed.

Treated end-of-line ⲭⲉ as ϫⲉ introducing direct discourse ('saying:') after ϯⲭⲱ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ ⲁⲣⲱⲧⲛ̄ 'I say it to you.' Line 8 then begins the imperative ⲱⲗ 'lift up, take up' (= ⲱⲗⲉ/ⲱⲗⲓ), governing ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'your heart' — a hortatory call to interior attention parallel to 'cast away from yourselves' that follows.

Translated 'cast away.' The verb (with ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth') functions as the soteriological complement to 'lift up your heart' — interior attention paired with renunciation. Etymology uncertain; possibly related to ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲑⲛⲉ 'discharge, expel.'

Translated 'practice' tentatively. The form is an abstract (ⲙⲛⲧ-) noun whose root ⲟⲁⲟⲩⲁⲛ is unidentified. Context places it parallel to 'garment of worship' and 'conducting-of-life (politeia)' — three terms for embodied participation in the dark spirits' realm. 'Practice/comportment' captures the parallel sense pending lexical parallels.
Translated 'their judgment.' Likely from ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon, judge' with nominal form ⲙⲡⲉ; paired here with ⲕⲟⲗⲁⲥⲓⲥ 'punishment.' Standard eschatological collocation 'judgment and punishment.'
Translated 'the Seventh.' ⲥⲁϣϩ is dialectal/scribal variant of ⲥⲁϣϥ 'seven'; ⲙⲁⲍ- is the ordinal prefix (= Sah. ⲙⲉϩ-). The flanking ⲍ̄ (numeral 7) confirms.

Translated 'were called forth' (passive of ⲧⲱϩⲙ̄ 'summon, call, invite, seal'). The serial-emanation formula 'one from another' shows that ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ here functions as the technical verb of cosmogonic emanation — each Father summoned/produced from the preceding one. Reused at line 26 (ⲁϩⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'he emanated').

Translated 'the Great Spirit.' Construction ⲡⲧⲛⲁⲟ + noun functions as 'the Great X' (cf. line 30 ⲡⲧⲛⲁⲟ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧ 'the Great Beloved'). This is the Mother of Life in Western Manichaean cosmology, the first emanation of the Father of Greatness.

Feminine forms (ⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ, ⲧⲉⲧⲁⲥⲉⲓ, ⲁⲥⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄) confirm that 'the Great Spirit' is grammatically feminine here, supporting the identification with the Mother of Life. Translated with feminine pronouns to preserve this.
Translated 'has been revealed.' ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ̄ here = ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ 'manifest, reveal'; the perfect ⲁϩ- prefix gives stative-perfect sense.
